attacks.text:
- Open its rear door, spawning several Infected Crews and Kraken Minions.
- Swing its eye, shoots 4 each in 4 directions that deals 3 damage. Each leaving a trail of 16 that moves at a moderate speed.
- Aims for 1-2 seconds before charging towards the player, dealing 4 damage. The attack direction can be seen with big purple marks (>>) on the floor.

tactics:
Try to stay behind the boss as much as possible, as this not only mitigates the torpedo attack because the torpedoes usually take large-angle turns when homing toward you, but you also get free oxygen when the moves.
Followers, Pets, & Bodyguards will be useful here, as they can take the bullets from the boss (but watch out for Followers: most WILL die if they take too much damage).
If the arena has no bullets or attack indicators from the Abyssal Submariner, don't assume that means you can sit still for very long: that could mean it's using the naval mine attack, so try to be light on your feet.
The sonar ping isn't necessarily bad, since if the Abyssal Submariner follows up with the sea mines, you can easily dodge them instead of accidentally running into one if you were unmarked. You just have to deal with the Weary ailment for a while.
When the boss summons its goons, prioritize killing them first, since they can be dangerous in large numbers: The Infected Crews can flood the arena with their bullets along with the boss, while Kraken Minions can drain your oxygen quickly.

name: Alien Aircraft Carrier
unique_attacks: 4 (9 with turrets in their functional state)

attacks.name: (chung)
attacks.text:
The boss has 4 external turrets which must be destroyed for its main body to become vulnerable. As long as the turrets are active their attacks will continue to fire off. Occasionally, the ship may shield one of its turrets and it must be broken through before it becomes susceptible to damage again. Turrets carry out unique attacks, which can be eliminated upon their destruction. 
Each time a turret is destroyed, the boss spawns enemies from the Spaceship biome, starting at 3, increasing by 1 for each subsequent lost turret and capping at 5.
After the boss' health gets below 50% for the first time, the player instantly gains 400 energy.

attacks.name: Side turrets
attacks.text:
The boss moves slightly leftwards or rightwards and fires a large laser beam from each of its side turrets, lasting 7 seconds and dealing 18 (19 in Badass mode) damage.
Even after the two turrets are broken, the boss will still be able to trigger this attack during the first phase.

attacks.name: Leftmost "body" turret
attacks.text:
The turret has two main possible attacks, which can sometimes trigger simultaneously:
- Continuously shoots concentric waves of bullets in all directions, lasting 12 seconds. Each bullet deals 15 (16) damage.
- Continuously shoots bullets in a spiral pattern in all directions, lasting 12 seconds. Each bullet deals 15 (16) damage.

attacks.name: Rightmost "body" turret
attacks.text:
The turret has two main possible attacks:
- Continuously fires one or two streams of square bullets in one or two directions, lasting 12 seconds. If there are two streams, they are separated by a 45° angle, so as to leave a considerable gap between them. Each bullet deals 15 (16) damage.
- Continuously fires a cone-shaped stream of square bullets at a 120° angle that targets the player as they move, lasting 12 seconds. Each bullet deals 15 (16) damage.

attacks.name: Core attacks
attacks.text:
All the following attacks can be triggered by the boss anytime. The boss can also summon several of these attacks simultaneously.
- Laser eye: shoots a continuous laser from its center, dealing 19 (20) damage and lasting 6 seconds. The laser homes on the player and can extend its range based on how far the player is from the boss.
- Homing missiles: Launches 6 homing missiles, each dealing 16 (17) damage. Each missile has a chance to inflict Burn, and the boss can launch several streams of missiles in a row.
- Expanding sphere: Generates a circular mass of lingering bullets, each dealing 14 (15) damage. If the player tries to break the bullets, they will regenerate. After 6 seconds, the ...

name: Baby Dragon Bros

attacks.name: (chung)
attacks.text:
As the name suggests, there are two dragons the player fights as the boss, the Grey and Black Dragons. The boss health bar consists of their cumulative HP, and they will attack independently from each other.
They attack at the same time throughout the fight, unless either of them got inflicted with Stun or Freeze.
A dragon will enrage once its health drops below half. Do note that each dragon will only drop 40 Energy once when enraged.

attacks.text:
- Fires arrowheads with a slight homing ability that deal 3 damage each. These deal a small explosion upon contact.
- Launches a spread of 3 big long arrows that generate eggs upon hitting a surface and deal 4 damage. These eggs will explode either after a delay or upon being struck.
- Fires a laser that sweeps the area. Deals 4 damage.
- Charges at the player, leaving a trail of eggs that explode after a delay or being struck.

attacks.name: Enraged Phase
attacks.text:
- Homing attacks are far more dense and used twice in one sitting.
- Spread attack fires 5 bullets instead of 3.
- Laser becomes wider, deals 5 damage, and is accompanied by a barrage of lasers rapidly fired in all directions that deal 2 damage each laser beam.

attacks.name: Normal Phase
attacks.text:
- Fires triangular bullets in every direction of its body, they hover in the air for a moment, before launching themselves at the player and deal 3 damage.
- Launches a spread of 3 big long bullets that generate fire pools on impact with a surface. Deal 4 damage on hit.
- Fires a laser that sweeps the area. Deals 4 damage.
- Charges at the player, leaving a trail of fire pools behind.

attacks.name: Enraged Phase
attacks.text:
- Ring attack is far more dense and is used twice in one sitting.
- Spread attack fires 5 bullets instead of 3.
- Laser becomes wider and deals 5 damage instead of 4.

tactics:
Do hide behind the pillars to avoid the incoming bullets and some of the missiles while regaining back the player's armor. The Fire Buff is immensely useful in this fight to negate fire damage from the fire pools and greatly reduce damage from the exploding eggs.
The lasers will definitely be the player's biggest problem, so be extra cautious around them. However, if the player plays as the Rogue, dodging can make the battle much easier, as the player can dodge the lasers with ease.
Keep the player's distance, as they cannot take their time with dealing with the boss. Focus on one dragon at a time to avoid enraging both of them at once.
Avoid using weapons that deal continuous damage (Laser Therapy, Double Therapy, etc.).
A long-range poke-and-run playstyle along with Statue of the Knight is recommended.
If the player is lucky enough to have One Punch, the player must be patient and try to strike only when both dragons are close to each other in order to maximize the damage. They do have quite significant speed, so try not to miss. However, due to their very deadly attacks, and by the fact that One Punch reduces speed for the first punch, it is very hard to do so. Trying to keep a distance from the Cave Ice Bug is not a very good idea as the obstacles may block the projectiles. Melee weapons are suitable and work even better if they don't consume energy - not only can they block ranged attacks, the player will have an effective form of offense against the boss at all times. Weapons capable of high burst damage, such as the Next-next-next-gen SMG, should be used during this vulnerability period.
Do not try to attack as soon as the fight starts. The shorter the boss is, the less time it takes to burrow underground. The attacks are not too dangerous if the player stands off the ice floor. Always be on the move; every aspect of the boss tends to be able to get the player at any point of the room. Just hiding behind a cover forever is not recommended, if there are actually any good ones. Especially in enraged phase, the player should instead run loops around the boss since some of the attacks go for single targets in a straight line. It's better if the player hugs along the walls, minimizing the massive areas of danger.
The help of a Follower would greatly ease the fight, since the player is not going to be the only one to absorb most of the damage coming from each attack.
Though it doesn't cause much problems, do keep an eye on the boss's shock wave attack since it has some different patterns and a very short cool down between each wave. It is likely to catch the player off-guard and deal constant damage to the player.

tactics:
Always watch its movement carefully. Don't shoot if it stops moving, because that means it's in its defensive form.
It is suggested that the player uses sniper rifles or slower firing weapons (with greater damage) instead of weapons like SMGs to have more control of their firing. This minimizes the boss' regeneration ability, because it only heals by 4 per shot regardless of the actual damage dealt.
Stay far away as much as possible, but do keep an eye on it so the player can avoid the surprise spike attacks. Fighting this boss mostly relies on their ability to safely move back and forth, especially around the covers and corners of the arena, to avoid getting hit.
Break the mines either to make sure they won't cause incorrect targeting or as a backup energy source for long-battle scenarios (be careful of the explosive barrels, however).

tactics:
Grand Knight has an excessive amount of projectile spam, so tackling him in the open is not recommended. The room does contain sufficient cover for the player to avoid them, and the fight is entirely dependent on the player's smart use of these obstacles.
If he remains at range and does not close in, ranged weapons work best as the player does not need to risk taking damage. The window of damaging him is small, requiring powerful bursts or a tedious attrition to eventually wear him down. Melee weapons are out of the picture but can be used to block his projectiles, or to inflict even more damage with the melee reflect buff.
When the boss is trapped within the cover walls, most of his projectiles will be blocked off. Players should exploit this period and unload everything they have at him.
Stalling is a valid option, giving the player more time to dodge his attacks before he can recover or to entirely demolish him before he can even retaliate. Even if he recovers, his attacks are not dangerous enough to entirely discourage the player from advancing.
